text:
mira: Heads-up — submitted a small PR to the provisioning handbook to add a worked example for tenant labeling, an SDK usage snippet, and a clearer SLA sentence. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4228 :paperclip:
ben: taking a look now. quick skim — love the example, but wording around 'isolation guarantees' might be strong. can we make that more precise?
sarah: +1 on wording. maybe say 'tenant isolation is preserved for reserved capacity; best-effort eviction policies apply to shared burst pools' — clearer and less absolutist.
priya: on the SDK snippet: I think the Python example should show the call that pins model version + scale policy. current snippet is a bit abstract. propose this short snippet:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(org_id="org-123")
resp = client.provision_tenant(
    tenant_id="team-alpha",
    model="ggml-13b-quant",
    reserved_gpus=2,
    isolation_level="reserved",
    rollout_policy={"canary_pct":5, "grace_period_s":600}
)
print(resp.status)
```
priya: also added a tiny terraform example for infra folks, to show reserved pool ref:```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "alpha" {
  name = "alpha-reserved"
  region = "us-west-2"
  gpus = 2
  isolation = "reserved"
}
```
docs-bot: CI check started for PR #4228 — linting, link-checker, and snippet-validate jobs queued.
ben: thanks priya, that SDK snippet looks good. can we make 'model' param more explicit about pinning semantics? e.g. model_version = "ggml-13b@2025-02-01" so people understand backcompat.
priya: yup, updated locally and pushed a commit. changed snippet to include model_version. also added a note about fallback policies for autoscale (how we fallback to compatible variant when reserved capacity is insufficient).
mira: nice. can we also add a short bullet in the handbook about SLA measurables — what counts as an incident vs. transient throttling? proposed wording: 'SLA uptime for Dedicated reserved pools is measured as availability of provisionable capacity for pinned tenants over a 30-day window; transient throttles (requests queued < 5s) are considered degraded but not SLA failures.' feedback?
eli: that wording seems tricky — ops team prefers using request rejection vs queued thresholds. maybe: 'SLA considers request rejections and sustained request latency above configured SLO thresholds as failures; short-lived queues (< 5s) are categorized as degraded performance.'
sarah: agree with eli. also add an example SLO table row in the doc: 99.9% availability for reserved pools, 99.5% for dedicated burst, with note about regional failover.
mira: good, I'll fold those edits in. one final ask — can someone sanity-check links to the autoscale policy page? I fixed two old anchors but not sure if the link-checker catches cross-repo refs.
docs-bot: link-checker reported one broken anchor: docs/autoscale#scale-policy-examples -> 404. CI failing.
ben: that anchor got renamed in the autoscale doc last month. quick fix: point to docs/autoscale#policy-schemas and add an inline note that examples moved.
priya: pushed the link fix and added a short migration note for teams migrating from legacy 'burst_pool' to 'reserved_pool' naming.
mira: thanks all — I'll re-run the PR checks. once CI passes can someone from eng-docs approve? want this in the handbook before next week's onboarding batch. :clock1:
ben: will approve after CI green and one more review on the SLA paragraph.
docs-bot: CI checks passed for PR #4228 — all jobs green.
ben: LGTM — approving.
mira: merged. tagging #release-notes to include a one-liner about tenant-handbook clarifications. :tada:
priya: awesome — adding a unit test to snippet-validate to ensure future autoscale anchor renames fail loudly.
eli: great follow-up. thanks everyone for quick turnaround.
